analysis:
Both units are BASE-side excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 6377-6792). The changed ranges are elsewhere in the file (head 453-473, 3239-3242, 3255-3286), so the supplied text does not contain the PR's modified lines. I reviewed the surrounding base text, which covers cluster memory refusal, MiMo/GLM tensor parallel, placement and the GPU-limit command. It is documentation only and no code or controls change in these units.

The visible text includes security-relevant statements that the PR's documented behavior may touch: sealed all-sum (AES-256-GCM on the keyed JACCL plane), load-agreement binding, tenant-partitioned prefix cache and encrypted SSD tier (T-041), and `darkbloom cluster gpu-limit` behind consent and an admin prompt (TB-014/T-062). I found no changes in these units that weaken them.

The PR patch excerpt (docs about a `darkbloom cluster stop` / `ClusterOnboardingStopped` stop-count mechanism, stopsAsked in the setup record and control reply) is truncated and describes new cross-Mac control behavior. The stop count is reported in a status reply, and the reply field is nil from older builds. I could not verify its authentication or its trust boundary (the pair's control channel, whether a peer can forge counts to abort onboarding, and the local command lock). That is a documentation claim only, with no implementation in evidence, so I record it as an unverified contract rather than a finding. Any follow-up should check the code behind ClusterControlReply.stopsAsked and OnboardingLive.stop for peer authentication and DoS exposure (availability of the pair setup, A-018-like). Because the modified head lines are not visible, I set needs_deeper_review to true.
